html:
Repair stations, parts shops and the port: is Miami NDT work under SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410?

Most aerospace NDT in Miami-Dade happens in repair stations rather than factories. Shops around Miami International Airport, in Doral, Medley, Miami Springs and Hialeah, overhaul landing gear, wheels, engine accessories, components and structure, much of it for Latin American and Caribbean operators. That changes how the certification question gets answered: the starting point is usually the station's own manual, not a purchase order. The national comparison of the two documents is in NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A.

Start with the repair station manual

Under Part 145 the FAA certificates the repair station; it does not certify the NDT technician. FAA Advisory Circular 65-31B (2014) lists NAS 410, ATA Specification 105, SNT-TC-1A, ISO 9712, CAN/CGSB-48.9712 and EN 4179 as acceptable standards, and each station states its choice in its manual. Two shops on the same Doral block can therefore certify inspectors to different documents and both be compliant. Ask the station's Level 3 which document and revision its program follows before you accept an offer.

When a customer or a foreign approval adds a layer

Contracts with airlines, lessors and component owners can name a personnel standard, and the station must then meet it for that work. A station that also holds an EASA Part-145 approval for European-registered aircraft should know that EASA's guidance points to EN 4179, the European twin of NAS 410. Repairs done under a manufacturer's program can bring that manufacturer's flow-down as well.

Component shops and parts makers are not the same case

Landing-gear, wheel and brake, and accessory shops use eddy current, penetrant and magnetic particle daily, following the inspection procedures in manufacturers' manuals, while the personnel standard behind the inspector remains the shop's choice under its manual and contracts. A company that manufactures parts and sells into airframe or engine supply chains sits in a different position. Its buyers usually write NAS 410 into the purchase-order quality clause, and that requirement flows down to every sub-tier shop that tests the hardware, with Nadcap AC7114 audits where the site is accredited.

Port Everglades, Turkey Point and the towers

Tank and piping inspection at Port Everglades and PortMiami, outage work at Florida Power & Light's Turkey Point site, and structural steel on high-rise and bridge projects run under written practices built on SNT-TC-1A, because the API, ASME and AWS documents behind that work call for it. A South Florida technician can certify on terminal piping one year and move into a hangar the next; the skill carries over, the certification does not.

Build a file the next Level 3 can credit

Under both schemes the employer certifies you and the certification ends with the job. What carries forward is evidence: course outlines with the hours recorded, a signed experience log split by method, examination results with the certification letters, and a current vision record. Moving into a NAS 410 program, expect the Responsible Level 3 (RL3) to ask for more formal penetrant and magnetic particle training than SNT-TC-1A recommends. In Miami's repair stations eddy current is often the method that decides a hire, so log those hours carefully.

For quality and accountable managers

Print the governing standard and its revision on every certification. If your manual adopts NAS 410, plan the move to Revision 6, released in December 2025, together with your customers, and update training material and examination banks at the same time. FAA inspectors, customer auditors and, for parts makers, Nadcap auditors read personnel files against what the manual promises. On the paperwork side, Atlantis can prepare and review the NAS 410 audit documentation your RL3 signs off. Separately, aviation NDT consulting from Atlantis builds written practices on SNT-TC-1A for repair stations and parts makers, aligned to the customer's flow-down and Nadcap AC7114.

Atlantis in South Florida

Atlantis training follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A: self-paced online theory with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions, rehearsal in the Practical NDT simulator, and the hands-on work and practical examination at your employer's facility under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in Miami. For repair-station work, see aviation NDT training and the method pages on eddy current testing in aviation and magnetic particle testing in aviation. Terminals and plants in Miami-Dade and Broward can engage Atlantis for UT, MT, PT and VT inspection.

So there is no confusion in Miami-Dade: Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3. If your station's program is written to NAS 410, its RL3 decides whether SNT-TC-1A-based training counts, so ask that person before enrolling.
